frase_gancho.texto: The city where, according to the Mexica, men become gods.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Teotihuacán was the great metropolis of the Classic period in the Central Highlands. Its name comes from Nahuatl, and it is usually translated as the place where men become gods. It was given by the Mexica, centuries after the city had been abandoned. It was laid out along two great axes, and the Avenue of the Dead was the main one. Artisans, merchants, and people who had come from other regions lived here. In this hall you will see the water goddess, a disk with a skull, braziers, and stone masks. There are also murals and the facade of the temple of the Feathered Serpent. Its ideas remained alive long after its fall.
